learningObjectives.title: Development of medicines and antibiotic resistance

options: A type of white blood cell
questions.explain: Pathogens (bacteria, viruses, fungi, protists) cause communicable disease.

options: Are caused by pathogens and can spread between organisms
questions.explain: Communicable (infectious) diseases spread; non-communicable ones do not.

questions.q: Which is a type of pathogen?
questions.explain: Pathogens include bacteria, viruses, fungi and protists.

questions.q: Non-communicable diseases such as heart disease:
options: Cannot be passed from person to person
questions.explain: Non-communicable diseases (e.g. cancer, heart disease) are not infectious.

questions.q: The skin defends the body mainly by:
questions.explain: Skin is a primary physical barrier against pathogens; stomach acid and mucus also defend.

questions.q: White blood cells defend against pathogens by:
questions.explain: Phagocytes engulf pathogens; lymphocytes produce antibodies and antitoxins.
Lymphocytes (a type of white blood cell) produce specific antibodies.

options: Introducing a weakened/inactive pathogen so the body makes antibodies and memory cells
questions.explain: Vaccines stimulate an immune response and memory cells for faster future responses.
Antibiotics kill or inhibit bacteria; they do not work against viruses.
Overuse selects for resistant bacteria, which survive and multiply.

questions.q: A patient stops taking antibiotics halfway through the course. The main risk is that:
options: Surviving bacteria may be resistant and multiply
questions.explain: Not completing the course can leave resistant bacteria, promoting resistance.

questions.q: New medicines are tested in clinical trials for:
questions.explain: Preclinical and clinical trials assess toxicity, efficacy and dosage.

questions.q: In a drug trial, a placebo is:
options: A dummy treatment with no active drug
A higher dose of the drug
questions.explain: Placebos help test whether effects are due to the drug itself.

options: Neither the patient nor the doctor knows who receives the real drug
questions.explain: Double-blind design reduces bias in assessing a drug's effects.

questions.q: A risk factor for non-communicable disease is:
questions.explain: Lifestyle risk factors include smoking, poor diet, alcohol and obesity.

questions.q: A malignant tumour differs from a benign tumour because it:
options: Can spread to other parts of the body
questions.explain: Malignant tumours (cancer) invade and spread (metastasise); benign tumours stay localised.

questions.q: Aseptic technique when culturing microorganisms is used to:
questions.explain: Sterile (aseptic) technique keeps cultures free from contamination.

questions.q: Public-health campaigns encouraging exercise and healthy diet aim to reduce:
questions.explain: Improving lifestyle lowers risk factors for non-communicable diseases.
